document_summary: Massachusetts General Laws c. 186, § 11, setting a fourteen-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease (Massachusetts statewide).

rules.title: M.G.L. c. 186 § 11 - Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: Fourteen days' written notice to quit is sufficient to end a written lease for nonpayment of rent, unless the tenant pays all rent due with interest and costs by the answer day in an eviction action.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies under a written lease where rent is neglected or refused.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: General notice-to-quit period for nonpayment; not a limit on grounds for eviction or non-renewal.
rules.extraction_notes: No effective date stated in the source text. Also provides that the court continues the hearing at least seven days where nonpayment was caused by a government payment delay.
